subject: Production incident: client-side streaming timeouts causing retry storms and elevated 5xx/429
messages:
From: Linda Park <linda.park@acme-health.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acme-health.com
Date: 2026-10-05T15:14:22-07:00
Subject: Production impact: streaming completions timing out -> rapid retries and 5xx spike

Sean —

We started seeing massive errors on our chat flows at ~14:45 PDT today. Client apps are hitting a client-side timeout and then rapidly retrying, which appears to have caused a retry storm against your streaming endpoint. Our monitoring shows a large spike in 5xx and 429 responses coming back from Redwood for the last 30 minutes. Throughput has degraded and users are getting fragmented responses or no response at all.

I attached a small sample trace and our client logs. We need immediate mitigation (circuit breaker or additional rate limiting) and a timeline for permanent fix. This is impacting our telehealth sessions right now.

Attaching: streaming-trace-20261005.jsonl, client-logs-acme-10-05.zip

Please escalate to engineering and execs if needed — Linda Park, VP Product, Acme Health

—
Linda Park
VP Product, Acme Health
linda.park@acme-health.com
From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>
To: Linda Park <linda.park@acme-health.com>
Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T15:22:10-07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: streaming completions timing out -> rapid retries and 5xx spike

Linda — thanks for the quick heads-up and for the logs. I’m escalating immediately. Marissa (CS) and Rishi (Eng) are on this thread.

Immediate actions we will take right now:
- Temporarily enable a stricter per-customer token rate-limit and short-lived circuit breaker on Acme traffic to reduce retry amplification.
- Block aggressive client retries from the trace patterns you shared (we can whitelist well-formed backoff semantics).
- Rishi will pull runtime traces and KV-cache stats to see if this is correlated to cache churn or kernel degradation.

I’ll confirm the temporary mitigation in the next 10–15 minutes and follow with a post-mortem timeline. Deeply sorry for the impact.

—
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
sean.gallagher@redwood.com
From: marissa.cole@redwood.com <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T15:24:40-07:00
Subject: Fwd: Production impact: streaming completions timing out -> rapid retries and 5xx spike

Looping in operations runbook snippet and our quick mitigation playbook. Rishi, please prioritize a short-lived kill switch + per-request backpressure on Acme’s model route. Also confirm if we should divert traffic to fallback model variants or region.

Ops checklist (doing now):
- Apply per-customer QPS cap (lower to 20 QPS) and 30s client connection limit.
- Enable streaming idle disconnect reasoning (idle-time TTL = 10s for now).
- Turn on extra logging for KV-cache hit/miss and batch sizes.

If we can get a 50% reduction in error amplification within 30 mins we can buy time to investigate the root cause.

—
Marissa Cole
Senior Customer Success Manager, Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.com
From: rishi.malhotra@redwood.com <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: marissa.cole@redwood.com, sean.gallagher@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-05T15:37:04-07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Production impact: streaming completions timing out -> rapid retries and 5xx spike

Team — quick write-up from initial investigation:
- Observed burst of short-lived streams from a small subset of Acme client IPs that match the provided client-logs. The pattern: open stream -> client aborts/writes timeout at ~4–6s -> immediate retry without exponential backoff.
- Runtime shows elevated KV-store miss rate and higher-than-normal batch flushes; that increases per-token latency under load.
- Several worker nodes hit transient OOM and restarted their runtime which generated 5xx responses for ~45 seconds during the spike window.

Immediate mitigations applied (15:30 PDT):
1) Per-customer circuit breaker enabled (QPS cap + 10s min backoff enforcement).
2) Idle stream disconnection lowered to 8s to free KV resources faster.
3) Blocklist of misbehaving client versions pushed (we identified a client that retries synchronously).

Next steps (post-stabilize):
- Safe fallback routing to lower-cost model variant for heavy streams while we stabilize kernels.
- Root cause: we need to reproduce the client retry loop under load. Requesting sample client container/versions from Acme to repro.
- Post-incident: propose a rate-limit contract clause and client SDK guidance for exponential backoff.

Attaching runtime snippet: streaming-trace-20261005.jsonl (pushed to shared drive).

—
Rishi Malhotra
Senior Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
From: Linda Park <linda.park@acme-health.com>
To: sean.gallagher@redwood.com, marissa.cole@redwood.com
Cc: ops@acme-health.com, support@acme-health.com
Date: 2026-10-05T16:05:44-07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: streaming completions timing out -> rapid retries and 5xx spike

Thanks for the rapid response and for applying a temporary throttle. We are still seeing degraded UX on some sessions, but error spikes have reduced a bit.

A few asks from our side:
- We need a short RCA for our SREs by EOD today and a remediation timeline.
- If you can provide an interim config that we can set in our client SDK to avoid immediate retries (we can push an emergency client patch), that would be ideal.
- We will need an executive update and written SLA remediation; this incident impacts our lead contract for telehealth sessions.

Please escalate to your leadership; I will be tracking internally as well.

—
Linda Park
VP Product, Acme Health
From: sean.gallagher@redwood.com <sean.gallagher@redwood.com>

Cc: marissa.cole@redwood.com, rishi.malhotra@redwood.com
Date: 2026-10-07T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Production impact: streaming completions timing out -> rapid retries and 5xx spike

Linda — follow-up and next steps.

Status: the temporary caps and blocklist held; error rate dropped ~70% and latency returned close to nominal for most flows. We still see intermittent client disconnections on a small Canary subset. Rishi’s team captured a reproducible scenario and a mitigation patch is scheduled to deploy tonight 23:00 PDT (kernel backpressure adjustment + safer KV-cache eviction policy).

Deliverables we’re providing today/tomorrow:
- EOD preliminary RCA doc (link: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/trace-20261005)
- Client SDK emergency config snippet for immediate deploy (exponential backoff sample + retry jitter) — I’ll send this in a separate email to your SRE alias.
- Formal exec note and remediation timeline will be sent by Marissa with proposed credit and SLA accommodations.

We appreciate the patience — Marissa will loop in our CS leadership to coordinate the exec update.

—
Sean Gallagher
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
